title: Trace delivery, redelivery, and broker pressure
description: Select a scenario to see what ActiveMQ Classic can observe, what the application must decide, and where a message waits when delivery cannot complete.

nodes.label: JMS producer
nodes.detail: Creates a message with a stable business event ID, destination, expiration policy, and persistence mode.

nodes.label: ActiveMQ broker
nodes.detail: Accepts messages, applies destination policy, dispatches to consumers, and enforces memory, store, and temporary-store limits.

nodes.label: KahaDB store
nodes.detail: Stores persistent messages for the local ActiveMQ Classic broker. Storage durability and broker high availability are separate design decisions.

nodes.label: JMS consumer
nodes.detail: Runs business logic and acknowledges or commits according to the session mode. A rollback, recovery, close-before-commit, or connection timeout can trigger redelivery.

nodes.label: Business store
nodes.detail: Commits the domain mutation and an event receipt together so repeated delivery produces one visible result.

nodes.label: Dead-letter queue
nodes.detail: Receives a poison message after the configured redelivery limit. Operators still need diagnosis, repair, bounded replay, and reconciliation.

scenarios.label: Healthy persistent delivery
scenarios.summary: The broker accepts and journals a persistent message, the consumer commits one business effect, then settles the JMS delivery.
scenarios.result: Settlement follows the durable business effect. This ordering narrows ambiguity, while a stable event receipt makes a later replay harmless.

scenarios.label: Timeout after business commit
scenarios.summary: The consumer commits the business mutation, but its connection times out before the broker observes successful settlement.
scenarios.result: Redelivery is correct because the broker cannot inspect the external database. The consumer must recognize the stable event ID and return the first result without applying a second mutation.

scenarios.label: Poison message
scenarios.summary: A permanent schema or business-rule failure repeats until the configured redelivery limit is exceeded.
scenarios.result: The dead-letter queue isolates repeatedly failing work; it does not fix it. Preserve identity, repair the cause, and replay at a bounded rate.

scenarios.label: Broker store pressure
scenarios.summary: Consumers fall behind until configured broker storage usage reaches its limit and producer flow control activates.
scenarios.result: A synchronous producer can block or fail according to policy. Raising the limit only delays the incident if sustained arrivals still exceed consumer service capacity.
